summary: Santo Pekoa International Airport (SON) serves Luganville on Espiritu Santo, the largest island in Vanuatu's archipelago and home to the country's second-largest city. Named after the nearby Mount Pekoa, the airport provides the primary gateway to one of the Pacific's most celebrated diving destinations and sites of significant World War II history. It handles both domestic flights connecting to Port Vila and limited international services, particularly from Australia and New Zealand.
faqs:
Q: What is the main purpose of Santo Pekoa International Airport?
A: It serves as the main gateway to Espiritu Santo Island, providing domestic connections to Port Vila and limited international flights from Australia and New Zealand.

Q: How far is the airport from Luganville city center?
A: The airport is located approximately 5 kilometers north of Luganville's town center, a short drive of around 10 minutes.

Q: Are there car rental services available at the airport?
A: Yes, several local rental companies offer vehicles at or near the airport, though booking in advance is recommended during peak tourist season.

Q: Can tourists arrange tours and diving excursions at the airport?
A: Most dive operators and tour companies arrange pickup from the airport or nearby accommodations in Luganville when bookings are made in advance.
transport_tips: Taxis and shared minibuses are available outside the terminal and can take you into Luganville or to nearby resorts. Rental cars are offered by local agencies, but arranging transportation through your accommodation in advance is often the most reliable option. Road conditions on Espiritu Santo vary, so confirm your destination before departing the airport.
local_tip: If visiting the famous Champagne Beach or blue holes, ask your hotel or a local guide about the best times to go—early morning visits often mean fewer crowds and better visibility for snorkeling and swimming.
